 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Player Stats

 Cameron Johnson finished with 19 points (7-of-13 FGs), three rebounds, six assists, two steals and two three-pointers against the Rockets on Friday.
 It has been another rough season in Denver for Johnson, but this was one of his best performances of the season, which included a new season high for assists. Johnson had a strong final season in Brooklyn, but he hasn’t been able to achieve that level of production during his two seasons as a Nugget. However, if he is able to provide lines like this, especially on a quieter night from Jamal Murray, Denver and fantasy managers will both be happy.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Cameron Johnson had an efficient 23 points (9-of-15 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, a steal and four 3-pointers in win over the Grizzlies. 
 Cameron Johnson has been much better in his second season’s with the Nuggets than he did last year. His ability to be a threat off of Jokic is something defenses have to respect. He won’t score 23 points and fill up the box score every night, but the Grizzlies struggled to defend him and he’ll have games like this every once in a while.

 All five Nuggets’ starters were upgraded from questionable to probable on Monday afternoon, and they’re now available. The Nuggets will roll out their usual starting five against the Rockets.

 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson accumulated 18 points (8-of-12 FGs), four rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Pacers. 
 Making his fifth appearance of the season, Johnson’s effort on Saturday was the best of the bunch. He shot 66.7 percent from the field, and his 18 points were a season high. Johnson has hit double figures in three of the four games he’s played since returning from an ankle injury that sidelined him for three games last month.

 Cameron Johnson finished with seven points (2-of-5 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, two steals and one three-pointer against the Trail Blazers on Monday. 
 Johnson checked out of this game with 1:08 remaining after appearing to tweak something in his left leg. Head coach David Adelman didn’t have an update after the game, so there isn’t any conclusion to draw at this point, other than Johnson could be hurt and miss time. If that happens, Trevon Brazile or Alpha Diallo will likely step into a starting role in place of Johnson.

 Jabari Smith Jr. finished with 21 points (7-of-8 FGs), four rebounds, three assists and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Friday.
 Following a hot start to the season, Smith has cooled down a bit in the month of November. This was his first time scoring at least 20 points in a game since Oct. 31, and he only did it because he was insanely efficient. Hopefully, his volume will start to tick back up so he can get back to being elite for fantasy managers, as he was in October. He’ll look to carry this production into their next matchup with the Clippers on Monday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Fred VanVleet lit up the Nuggets with 25 points (10-of-21 FGs), one rebound, nine assists, one steal and three three-pointers on Friday.
 Despite missing all of last season, VanVleet has still been solid in fantasy basketball so far this year. He was able to set a new season high for scoring in this game, making this the first time he scored at least 25 points in a game since March of 2025. VanVleet’s presence in the lineup has been huge for Houston this year, and he proved in this game that he’s still capable of big scoring nights, even if they aren’t going to come consistently.

 Luka Dončić put up 25 points (9-of-18 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, two steals, two 3-pointers, and six turnovers in the 106-104 win over the Kings. 
 Luka continues to dominate the game and the Kings couldn’t do much to stop him. In the clutch, Keegan Murray did get a steal on him which could’ve cost the Lakers the game. You would wish the turnover numbers go down, but with the load that he’s had to do on offense, it’s hard to complain too much. He’s dominating everyone else from a statistical basis that is helping you in other areas. 
 -  Brian Taylor

 Alperen Şengün led the Rockets with 28 points (9-of-16 FGs, 9-of-13 FTs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in a 133-124 loss to the Nuggets on Friday.
 Şengün recorded his second triple-double of the season, but it wasn’t enough for Houston to secure the win. It has been a fantastic season for Şengün so far, as he is currently averaging career highs in points, assists, three-pointers and free throw percentage. He has been on the cusp of this type of production over the last few seasons, and it seems like he’s finally reaching it. The Rockets have started the season well, and Şengün has been right at the center of it.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Christian Braun lit up the Rockets with 19 points (7-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, four steals, one block and three three-pointers in a 133-124 win on Friday.
 Last year was a down one for Braun, but he has bounced back to start this season. The offense is starting to pick up, but it’s his defensive impact that has been the biggest difference. He has at least one steal in every game this season and has had two or more in 10 of his 14 games, which has led to his career-high 2.3 steals per game. That’s carrying his category league value right now, which means he’s mostly been a one-trick pony, though he has been decent in a few other categories.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Grimes started off slowly but got going later in the game and helped the Lakers hold on. He’s still worth holding, but coach JJ Reddick did say that he’s hoping to have Austin Reaves back on Monday against the Jazz, or on Friday against the San Antonio Spurs.  Walker Kessler put up 15 points (7-of-11 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, a steal, and three blocks, and a three in the win over the Kings. 
 Kessler had a very good game despite being in foul trouble. He had his way with Sabonis being in the paint and put up some good numbers.  DeMar DeRozan provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (4-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, two assists and one steal against the Rockets on Friday.
 DeRozan started this season scoring in double figures in each of Denver’s first three games. In the 10 games since, he has only scored in double figures three more times. The positive news is that he’s reached that mark in back-to-back games. DeRozan isn’t going to provide value anywhere near what he has throughout his career, but if he can continue to be a reliable bench scorer for Denver, he’ll be a valuable piece for this team when the playoffs arrive.

 Sabonis continues to chug along and be efficient from the field. He did a good job on the offensive end and helping keep the Kings in the game, but he didn’t do a good job preventing Walker Kessler from having a good game. He at least got more shot attempts in this game after it’s been lackluster for the past few games.
